summary: SSH certificate provisioning failure after Okta attribute mapping change blocks DB-admin runbooks
description:
Issue summary:
On 2026-03-12 at ~09:20 UTC, multiple DB-admin runbooks that rely on automated SSH certificate issuance via the ssh-cert-service began failing. Affected engineers reported immediate 'permission denied' from bastion and the cert service returning 400/422 errors indicating missing attributes.

Impact:
- ~12 engineers could not complete critical DB maintenance runbooks for production clusters in us-west.
- Automated emergency playbooks that reissue short-lived certs blocked, causing temporary operational degradation during a scheduled maintenance window.
- No external customer impact, but internal incident prevented timely DB roll-forward fixes.

Environment:
- prod-us-west (bastion cluster: bastion-usw-1)
- ssh-cert-service v1.4.2 (container image sha: sha256:...f3a1)
- Okta SCIM connector (custom) -> identity-provisioner v2.1.0

Steps to reproduce (summary):
1) Request SSH cert via internal portal (https://internal.redwood/ssh-cert) for an account that should have 'sshAccess' group claim.
2) ssh-cert-service returns 422 with payload: "missing required claim: sshAccess".
3) Manually inspect Okta user profile via Admin Console and SCIM attribute mapping shows 'sshAccess' mapping updated 09:15 UTC.

Relevant logs / excerpts: 
- ssh-cert-service stderr:
  2026-03-12T09:19:20Z ERROR http request id=tx-9c3 MissingClaimError: required claim "sshAccess" not present for user jdoe@redwood
  2026-03-12T09:19:20Z WARN http request id=tx-9c3 user-info: {"okta_id":"00u1abcd...","groups":[]}
- Okta SCIM connector logs (identity-provisioner):
  2026-03-12T09:15:04Z INFO scim mapping reload applied from ui change id=ui-attr-547
  2026-03-12T09:15:05Z ERROR scim sync user=jdoe failed: attribute sshAccess not found in source mapping

Initial hypothesis:
- A recent manual change in Okta attribute mapping UI removed or renamed the 'sshAccess' group-to-claim mapping. SCIM connector reloaded the mapping which caused downstream tokens/user-info to not include the sshAccess claim. The ssh-cert-service enforces presence of that claim to authorize cert issuance.

Investigation notes:
- Confirmed mapping change in Okta audit log at 09:15 UTC by admin 'ops-admin' (ticketed as internal change).
- Reproduced condition by reloading scim connector in staging with the altered mapping and observed identical 422 responses.
- Verified that older cached tokens issued before 09:15 still worked for ~5m due to token TTL and allowed a small number of certs to be issued post-change.
- Identified ~12 distinct engineers whose accounts had group membership present in Okta but missing in the userinfo returned to ssh-cert-service.
- Correlated with a recently deployed PR in identity-provisioner (pr/2134) that added stricter claim validation; that combined with mapping removal caused immediate failure instead of previous soft-fail behavior.

Temporary mitigation performed:
- Rolled back Okta attribute mapping to the previous configuration at 09:34 UTC (rollback performed by Ops oncall: Marco Rivera).
- Restarted identity-provisioner pods to force a fresh SCIM sync and mapping reload (kubectl rollout restart deploy/identity-provisioner -n infra).
- Manually reissued stale tokens for affected users via internal admin token refresh tool to ensure they regained access while sync converged.

Resolution summary:
- Root cause: accidental Okta attribute mapping change that removed the 'sshAccess' mapping + recent claim-validation hardening in identity-provisioner (pr/2134) causing cert issuance to reject users missing the claim.
- Fix: Rolled back the Okta mapping and deployed a patch to identity-provisioner (pr/2134 -> pr/2150) to add a short grace window where missing non-critical claims are logged but do not block cert issuance for 10m after mapping changes.
- Verified: All affected engineers confirmed they could obtain certificates by 10:10 UTC and runbooks completed successfully.

Follow-ups / action items:
- #1: Create a small preflight check in identity-provisioner to detect mapping changes and alert Slack channel #auth-ops before the mapping is applied. (Owner: Marco Rivera)
- #2: Add an automated smoke test for ssh-cert-service in the post-deploy pipeline to prevent regressions from claim-validation changes. (Owner: DevEx)
- #3: Update the SSH Cert Rotation runbook with steps for manual reissue and Okta rollback checklist. (Owner: SRE Documentation)
- #4: Conduct a short training with the Ops team on Okta attribute mapping UI to avoid accidental edits. (Owner: IAM team)

2026-03-12 09:35 - Aisha Patel (reporter): Confirmed running manual reissue for user set; still seeing 401 on two accounts (re-run after restart).
2026-03-12 09:40 - SRE Pager (automated): Alert cleared for ssh-cert-service 5xx spike after restart. Noted partial 422s while SCIM converged.
2026-03-12 10:05 - Jane Liu (DB eng): All DB runbook steps completed successfully. Thanks oncall.

2026-03-14 14:12 - Marco Rivera: Deployed identity-provisioner patch pr/2150 which adds mapping-diff grace behavior and alerting hook. Added follow-ups in backlog INT-864210 (docs/update-runbook) and INT-864211 (smoke-tests).
resolution: Rolled back Okta attribute mapping; restarted identity-provisioner to re-sync groups; deployed a targeted patch to identity-provisioner to allow short grace period for claim propagation; manual reissue for affected accounts. Follow-up tasks created for runbook updates and preflight checks.
notes: This incident highlights a common failure mode at the Okta -> SCIM -> service boundary. Recommend limiting direct UI edits in Okta for mapping changes and routing such changes through an IAM change process with automated preflight checks.
